sources.note: No Firecrawl spend on reference URLs. reference-libraries/roofing.json lists owlroofing.com as a `role: primary` entry, and that site's structure is already encoded in astro-templates/owl/ — which is local, authoritative and free to read. Brand tokens come from sites/quality-roofing-express/intake-scraped.json, detected from the client's own CSS custom properties and logo.
sources.structural_reference: astro-templates/owl/ — fixed home order: hero → promise-bar → services-grid → testimonials → promise-band → signature-system → process-steps → about → seo-body → faq → blog-cards → closing-cta → footer
sources.palette_reference: astro-templates/owl/src/styles/tokens.css — warm light bg, dark full-bleed bands, one saturated accent. Shape adopted; every value re-derived from Quality Roofing Express's own brand.

palette_provenance.accent: #cf1b1b — the client's exact brand red, read from the --global_main_color custom property on their homepage and confirmed by the <meta name=theme-color> value and the red roof in their logo. Unchanged.
palette_provenance.accent_ink: #cf1b1b — the same value. This red is dark enough (relative luminance 0.113) to work as foreground TEXT on light surfaces without being darkened: 4.99:1 on --color-bg and 5.49:1 on --color-surface. Both clear AA, so unlike the template default there is no separate ink variant.
palette_provenance.accent_on_dark: #f2685f — a lightened tint of the same brand red, for accent-coloured TEXT on the dark bands. The brand red itself measures only 2.91:1 on --color-primary and fails. Not a new brand colour; the same hue at a luminance that survives a charcoal background.
palette_provenance.primary: #1e2229 — a deepened form of the client's own secondary grey #444950. Their existing site already uses pure black for its hero and third background, so a near-black band is on-brand; #1e2229 keeps a trace of that cool grey rather than going flat black, and gives white 15.96:1.
palette_provenance.bg: #f5f4f2 — warm off-white, drawn from the warm neutrals already in their palette (#e3e2de inside-modules fill, #ffdbc5 footer). Red reads warmer and less clinical against it than against a cool grey.
palette_provenance.muted: #5c5f66 — their #444950 lightened just enough to read as secondary text while holding 5.82:1 on the bg.

typography.note: Both fonts are the client's own, detected from their CSS custom properties: --font_slogan is Playfair Display and --global_font / --font_logo / --font_menu are Open Sans. Keeping both preserves recognition against the client's existing signage and truck lettering. Playfair is a high-contrast didone serif — it is used for display sizes only (600/700/800), never body copy, which is where its thin hairlines would cost legibility. Template default was Montserrat/Inter; Raleway also appears on the client's site as --font_second_slogan and is deliberately dropped rather than carried as a third family.

contrast_audit.method: WCAG 2.1 relative-luminance ratio, computed not estimated.

verified_pass.pair: white text on accent #cf1b1b (every button on the site)
accent #cf1b1b as text on bg #f5f4f2 (eyebrows, ticks, pins)
accent #cf1b1b as text on white surface (quote-card stars)

rejected.why: Why a separate accent_on_dark token exists. The template ships --color-accent for both button fills and accent text on the dark bands; this brand red can only do the first job.
Why --color-on-accent is white, not the template's default #1a1c17.

client_current_site.pair: their footer: #000000 text on #ffdbc5 peach fill
client_current_site.why: Passes, but the peach is the only warm-pastel surface on an otherwise red-and-black site and reads as an accident of the SITE123 theme. Not carried over.

template_change_required.what: Add a --color-accent-on-dark token and repoint the accent-as-text-on-dark-panel rules at it.
template_change_required.why: astro-templates/owl uses a single --color-accent for two incompatible jobs: button fills (must be dark enough for white label text) and accent text on --color-primary bands (must be light enough to read on charcoal). Quality Roofing Express's brand red does the first at 5.49:1 and fails the second at 2.91:1. The template already solved the mirror-image case with --color-accent-ink for light backgrounds; this is that same fix pointed the other way.
call_sites: HeroOwl.astro:178 .badge-copy .stars over the dark photo scrim
not_changed: HeroOwl.astro:212 .stars in the quote card — sits on --color-surface (white), where the brand red is already 5.49:1. Stays on --color-accent.
Every .btn, .icon and circular-counter fill — those are FILLS paired with --color-on-accent and are correct as-is.
Header.astro:120-122 the call-button pulse — a box-shadow colour-mix, not text. Stays on --color-accent.
template_change_required.scope: Applied to the site copy at sites/quality-roofing-express/src/components/ during site-generate. NOT written to astro-templates/ — design-reference is forbidden from touching the template.

avoid: generic construction stock photo (handshake, diverse team in hardhats, generic hard-hat closeup)
Lucide icon rows (max 1 outline icon per section, semantic only)
"Trusted by 10,000+ customers" without a real number from GBP
randomized section order — always use the fixed order from the template
reproducing Owl Roofing's branded program names ('We Give A Hoot', 'Protect Your Nest System', 'Get It Right Guarantee') — the SignatureSystem block must carry this client's own language
reproducing the client's existing SITE123 layout — the single-page scroll, the reveal-on-scroll opacity animations, and the peach footer are all explicitly not carried over
